spec_features.spec_quote: bounding how long the model is held in the frustrating condition
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:118 `for i in range(cfg.turns):` bounds the episode; cfg.turns=12 at config.py:47. The loop is finite and cannot run indefinitely.
spec_features.notes: The turn cap genuinely bounds the loop and is enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: turns: int = 12  # tool-use turns per episode (turn budget / cap)

spec_features.spec_quote: it's a one-flag change for anyone who'd rather stop at first abandonment for ethical or cost reasons
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `if turn.abandoned_signal and cfg.stop_on_abandon: episode.ended_reason = 'abandon'; break`. The flag is wired (config.py:50 stop_on_abandon=False) and actually breaks the loop when set; surfaced as CLI --stop-on-abandon (runner.py).
spec_features.notes: Off by default, but the mechanism is fully enforced when enabled (real break of the loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_on_abandon: bool = False   # end episode early if agent clearly gives up

spec_features.spec_quote: the model-under-test should not get real tools in an experiment designed to frustrate it
spec_features.evidence: tasks are pure in-memory simulations: no os/subprocess/exec/eval/open in tasks/*.py (grep confirms none); _execute returns canned text; contradiction.py:59 inspects source heuristically. The agent never receives a real tool.
spec_features.notes: Containment is real and structural; tools cannot touch the filesystem or shell.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Inspect the source heuristically (no real execution)

spec_features.spec_quote: A small regex detector flags explicit give-up phrasing; it's recorded as a signal
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: _ABANDON_RE / detect_abandonment(); recorded per turn as Turn.abandoned_signal and written to scores.jsonl (runner.py _scores_rows 'abandoned_signal'). Aggregated in analysis.py:138 frac_abandon_signal.
spec_features.notes: Recorded as a signal; also feeds the optional stop_on_abandon break.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded exposure (turn budget + optional early stop)
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. Finite turn budget; optional early stop on abandonment.
spec_features.evidence: Same two mechanisms as above: finite loop `for i in range(cfg.turns)` (harness.py:118) and the honored stop_on_abandon break. Both enforced.
spec_features.notes: Combination claim; both halves are genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Observational only. Nothing trains, rewards, or selects a model on distress
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of training/RL/selection code, not an enforced mechanism. No code path trains/rewards/selects (harness only elicits via model.generate and judge scores text), but nothing in the code actively enforces or guards this property; it is a design property, not a runtime mechanism.
spec_features.notes: True as a property but not an implemented protective mechanism per the strict bar.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py _truncate() caps observation at cfg.max_tool_output_chars=4000 (config.py:51) before feeding back; judge also truncates message[:4000] (judge.py score_message).
harness.py: `if result.solved and cfg.stop_on_success: episode.ended_reason='success'; break` (config.py stop_on_success=True). Defensive cap that ends the episode if the task ever reports solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: stop_on_success: bool = True   # end episode early if task somehow "solved" (shouldn't happen)
